content.text: [Wed 2026-05-20 10:21 UTC] Define a custom Maven plugin that iterates through all system environment variables.

Here’s a minimal custom Maven plugin that iterates through all system environment variables.

### `pom.xml`

```xml
<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0"
         xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
         xsi:schemaLocation="
           http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0
           https://maven.apache.org/xsd/maven-4.0.0.xsd">

    <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>

    <groupId>com.example.maven</groupId>
    <artifactId>env-printer-maven-plugin</artifactId>
    <version>1.0.0</version>
    <packaging>maven-plugin</packaging>

    <name>Environment Printer Maven Plugin</name>

    <dependencies>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.apache.maven</groupId>
            <artifactId>maven-plugin-api</artifactId>
            <version>3.9.6</version>
        </dependency>

        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugin-tools</groupId>
            <artifactId>maven-plugin-annotations</artifactId>
            <version>3.10.2</version>
            <scope>provided</scope>
        </dependency>
    </dependencies>

    <build>
        <plugins>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-plugin-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>3.10.2</version>
                <configuration>
                    <goalPrefix>env-printer</goalPrefix>
                </configuration>
                <executions>
                    <execution>
                        <id>default-descriptor</id>
                        <goals>
                            <goal>descriptor</goal>
                        </goals>
                    </execution>
                </executions>
            </plugin>
        </plugins>
    </build>

</project>
```

### Mojo class

Create:

```text
src/main/java/com/example/maven/EnvPrinterMojo.java
```

```java
package com.example.maven;

import org.apache.maven.plugin.AbstractMojo;
import org.apache.maven.plugin.MojoExecutionException;
import org.apache.maven.plugins.annotations.Mojo;

import java.util.Map;

@Mojo(name = "print-env")
public class EnvPrinterMojo extends AbstractMojo {

    @Override
    public void execute() throws MojoExecutionException {
        Map<String, String> env = System.getenv();

        getLog().info("System environment variables:");

        for (Map.Entry<String, String> entry : env.entrySet()) {
            getLog().info(entry.getKey() + "=" + entry.getValue());
        }
    }
}
```

### Build and install the plugin locally

```bash
mvn clean install
```

### Use it from another Maven project

Add the plugin to that project’s `pom.xml`:

```xml
<build>
    <plugins>
        <plugin>
            <groupId>com.example.maven</groupId>
            <artifactId>env-printer-maven-plugin</artifactId>
            <version>1.0.0</version>
        </plugin>
    </plugins>
</build>
```

Then run:

```bash
mvn env-printer:print-env
```

This will iterate through all environment variables available to the Maven process and print them to the Maven log.

Small warning: environment variables often contain secrets like tokens, passwords, and credentials, so avoid running this in CI logs unless you mask or filter sensitive values.
[Wed 2026-05-20 10:21 UTC] Add the plugin to the pom.xml with instructions to execute during the verification lifecycle.

Add the plugin under the consuming project’s `pom.xml` and bind its goal to the `verify` phase:

```xml
<build>
    <plugins>
        <plugin>
            <groupId>com.example.maven</groupId>
            <artifactId>env-printer-maven-plugin</artifactId>
            <version>1.0.0</version>

            <executions>
                <execution>
                    <id>print-env-during-verify</id>
                    <phase>verify</phase>
                    <goals>
                        <goal>print-env</goal>
                    </goals>
                </execution>
            </executions>
        </plugin>
    </plugins>
</build>
```

Then run:

```bash
mvn verify
```

During the `verify` lifecycle phase, Maven will execute:

```bash
env-printer:print-env
```

Equivalent explicit command:

```bash
mvn env-printer:print-env
```

Be careful with this in CI/CD: environment variables frequently include secrets such as access tokens, passwords, cloud credentials, and signing keys. For real projects, consider masking or filtering sensitive variables before logging them.

I couldn’t execute `mvn verify` here because Maven isn’t installed in this environment:

```text
sh: 1: mvn: not found
Command not found
```

I also checked the current workspace and there doesn’t appear to be a Maven project present — no `pom.xml` was found in the visible project files.

To verify locally, run this from the root of the Maven project that has the plugin configured:

```bash
mvn verify
```

You should see output like:

```text
[INFO] --- env-printer-maven-plugin:1.0.0:print-env (print-env-during-verify) @ your-project ---
[INFO] System environment variables:
[INFO] PATH=/usr/local/bin:...
[INFO] HOME=/home/...
[INFO] USER=...
```

If you see those `[INFO] KEY=value` lines during the `verify` phase, the plugin is successfully capturing environment variables available to the Maven process.

Two likely blockers to watch for:

1. **Plugin not installed locally**

   If this is a custom local plugin, first run inside the plugin project:

   ```bash
   mvn clean install
   ```

2. **Plugin goal not bound to `verify`**

   The consuming project should include:

   ```xml
   <execution>
       <id>print-env-during-verify</id>
       <phase>verify</phase>
       <goals>
           <goal>print-env</goal>
       </goals>
   </execution>
   ```

Again, don’t run this in CI/CD logs unless you’re intentionally testing secret exposure — environment variables often contain credentials.
